facts.fact_text: All the applicants accepted that they had participated in legally organised demonstrations.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 17 December 2005 with the authorisation of the governor's office.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 19 February 2006 with the authorisation of the governor's office.
At the hearing on 18 May 2006, the applicants conceded before the Ankara Assize Court that they had participated in the demonstration of 17 December 2005.
At the hearing on 18 May 2006, the applicants conceded before the Ankara Assize Court that they had participated in the demonstration of 19 February 2006.
At the hearing on 18 May 2006, the applicants stressed that the demonstrations of 17 December 2005 and 19 February 2006 had been legal.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and SGD (Socialist Youth Association) members had been holding legally authorised demonstrations in favour of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) on the pretext of exercising their democratic rights.
The Ankara Assize Court noted that all the applicants except Selçuk Mart had participated in the demonstration of 17 December 2005.
The Ankara Assize Court observed that Selçuk Mart had attended the demonstration of 19 February 2006.
On 6 March 2006 the applicants were taken into police custody.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Levent Çakır.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Deniz Bakır.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Alihan Alhan.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Necla Çomak.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Metin Kürekçi.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Latife Canan Kaplan.
On 7 March 2006 the Ankara Assize Court ordered the detention of Uğur Güdük.
On 22 March 2006 the Ankara public prosecutor filed an indictment with the Ankara Assize Court against the applicants.
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Deniz Bakır of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Metin Kürekçi of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Necla Çomak of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Alihan Alhan of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
Metin Kürekçi was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Necla Çomak was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Alihan Alhan was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Deniz Bakır was sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The remaining applicants (other than Deniz Bakır, Metin Kürekçi, Necla Çomak and Alihan Alhan) were convicted on 17 January 2007 of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The remaining applicants convicted of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation were each sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
On 22 October 2008 the Ankara Assize Court issued a judgment containing the same conclusions and sentences as in its judgment of 17 January 2007.
The Ankara Assize Court convicted Metin Kürekçi, Necla Çomak, Alihan Alhan and Deniz Bakır under Articles 220 § 7 and 314 §§ 2 and 3 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

Levent Çakır, Uğur Güdük, Latife Canan Kaplan, Serdar Kır, Selçuk Mart, Mehmet Ali Tosun, Filiz Uluçelebi and Mesut Açıkalın were convicted pursuant to section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (Prevention of Terrorism Act).
On 1 April 2005 Law no. 5237 (the Turkish Criminal Code) entered into force.

At the material time, Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who aids an illegal organisation knowingly and willingly, even if he does not belong to the hierarchical structure of the organisation, shall be punished as a member of the organisation.

Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that anyone who becomes a member of an armed organisation mentioned in Article 314 § 1 shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of between five and ten years.

Article 314 § 3 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that other provisions relating to the crime of establishing an organisation for the purpose of criminal activity are also applicable to the crime of membership of an armed organisation under Article 314.

In its Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002, the Venice Commission noted that according to non-governmental sources, in the application of Article 314 of the Turkish Penal Code, domestic courts in many cases decide on the membership of a person in an armed organisation on the basis of very weak evidence, raising questions as to the 'foreseeability' of the application of Article 314.

Mr Thomas Hammarberg stated in his report of 10 January 2012 that the provisions contained in the Turkish anti-terror legislation and Article 220 of the Turkish Criminal Code allow for a very wide margin of appreciation, in particular in cases where membership in a terrorist organisation has not been proven and when an act or statement may be deemed to coincide with the aims or instructions of a terrorist organisation.

The Human Rights Watch report of 1 November 2010 stated that Turkish Penal Code Articles 220/6 and 220/7 are so vaguely worded and lacking in clarity about what is prohibited as to offer an individual no indication of how to regulate or limit conduct.

The Human Rights Watch report of 1 November 2010 recommended that the Turkish Government urgently amend Turkish Penal Code Article 220 and repeal Articles 220/6 and 220/7, which are vague, lack legal clarity and specificity, and are therefore subject to arbitrary application.
The applicants were taken into police custody on suspicion of aiding and abetting the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).
The MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) was classified as an illegal armed organisation.
The applicants were mainly questioned about their participation in a number of demonstrations.
Metin Kürekçi was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Necla Çomak was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Alihan Alhan was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Deniz Bakır was sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The remaining applicants convicted of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation were each sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and SGD (Socialist Youth Association) members had been holding legally authorised demonstrations in favour of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) on the pretext of exercising their democratic rights.
The Ankara Assize Court found it established that the applicants had chanted the slogan 'M-L-K-P' during the demonstration held on 17 December 2005.
The Ankara Assize Court found it established that the applicants had chanted the slogan 'Yaşasın partimiz MLKP' ('Long live our Party, MLKP') during the demonstration held on 17 December 2005.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that the applicants had chanted the slogan 'Devrimin zaferi, biji MLKP' ('Victory to the revolution, long live the MLKP') during the demonstration held on 17 December 2005.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that the applicants had chanted the slogan 'İşçiler partiye, MLKP'ye' ('Workers join the party, join the MLKP') during the demonstration held on 17 December 2005.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that Necla Çomak had chanted the slogan 'Yaşasın 1. Kürdistan konferansı' ('Long live the first Conference of Kurdistan') during the demonstration of 17 December 2005.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established that Uğur Güdük had chanted the slogan 'Yaşasın 1. Kürdistan konferansı' ('Long live the first Conference of Kurdistan') during the demonstration of 17 December 2005.
The Ankara Assize Court noted that Selçuk Mart had chanted the slogan 'Dısa dısa serhildan MLKP Kürdistan' ('Rise up again and again, MLKP Kurdistan') during the demonstration of 19 February 2006.

The Ankara Assize Court found that the acts of Levent Çakır, Uğur Güdük, Latife Canan Kaplan, Serdar Kır, Selçuk Mart, Mehmet Ali Tosun, Filiz Uluçelebi and Mesut Açıkalın had constituted propaganda in favour of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) and thereby propaganda inciting people to commit violence or other methods of terrorism.

Amnesty International, in its 2013 Report on Turkey, considered that conduct which is not in itself criminal, such as activity related to the exercise of the rights to freedom of assembly, association and expression, is considered as evidence of membership of defendants in an armed organisation by Turkish courts.

Amnesty International's 2013 Report on Turkey stated that individuals have been prosecuted for membership of a terrorist organisation on charges relating solely to their engagement in peaceful and, in themselves, lawful pro-Kurdish activities.

In its Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002, the Venice Commission noted that the European Court of Human Rights applied the same principle in the case of Gül and Others v. Turkey (application no. 4870/02) and held that the criminal conviction of the applicants on the basis of Article 169 of the former Turkish Penal Code constituted an interference with their right to freedom of expression, since the only evidence used against them was the content of the slogans they shouted during a public demonstration.

The Amnesty International report of 27 March 2013 stated that no inference should be drawn from someone undertaking a lawful act, such as participating in a peaceful demonstration, even if such acts benefit, through lawful means, goals shared by a terrorist organisation.
